title: Image Array Processing
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of image array processing and name one situation where it is useful.
Apply image dimensions and channels to a small NumPy example and inspect the resulting values, shape, or dtype.
Identify one important limitation, boundary case, or validation check for image array processing.

content.intro: This lesson develops topic 213 of the supplied curriculum: **Image Array Processing**. The main starting point is **Image dimensions and channels**. You will connect the idea to a small, synthetic example, then use the result to reason about shape, dtype, accuracy, or memory as appropriate.
content.why_it_matters: An analysis workflow is a chain of explicit stages: validate input, clean data, apply numerical operations, summarize results, and save enough metadata to reproduce the output.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Treat **Image Array Processing** as an explicit step in an array workflow. This lesson centers on **Image dimensions and channels** and the source syllabus's related subtopics. Before trusting a result, identify the input shape and dtype, perform the smallest useful operation, and inspect the output. The example uses synthetic data so you can change one value and observe what changes.

content_blocks.code:
import numpy as np

image = np.array([[[10, 20, 30], [40, 50, 60]]], dtype=np.uint8)
image_crop = image[:, :1, :]
print(image.shape, image_crop.shape)

common_mistakes.problem: Cleaning data without recording the rule
common_mistakes.why: Different filtering assumptions can materially change the results.
common_mistakes.fix: Document thresholds, missing-data treatment, and excluded rows.
